Board heading: 14.5 The Chain Rule

Theorem · The Chain Rule (Simplest Case)

Let be a differentiable function of and , where and are differentiable functions of . Then is a differentiable function of , and

Explanation (added)

depends on in two ways, through and through , and the formula has one product for each: (how fast changes with ) × (how fast changes with ), plus the same through . The tree below draws this: each term is one path from down to , multiplying the derivatives along the way. Stewart calls this Case 1 (§14.5 Theorem 1, p. 985). What a typical exam question looks like
  • Find with the Chain Rule, often at a particular , like at in Section 4; sometimes also by substituting first and differentiating, as a check (Stewart §14.5 Exercises 1–8).
  • Find and when and depend on and , like in Section 6 (Exercises 9–16).
  • Write out the Chain Rule for a given set of dependencies using a tree diagram (Exercises 21–24).
  • Find a partial derivative at given values, like at , , in Section 8: compute first, then plug in (Exercises 25–30), or use a table of values of the functions and their derivatives (Exercises 17–20).
  • Use to find (Exercises 31–34), or , (Exercises 35–38), as in Sections 10 and 11.
  • Theory: state a version of the Chain Rule, or prove the simplest case (the argument in Section 3).
